text: Welcome to America's Town Meeting from New York City.
Tonight's subject, flying saucers, fact or illusion.
Our speakers are Major Donald E. Keogh, author of Flying Saucers from Outer Space,
and Jonathan N. Leonard, science editor of Time Magazine and author of Flight Into Space.
For scores of generations, civilized men have recorded astonishing descriptions of atmospheric phenomena and awesome things hovering in the skies above them.
Mysterious floating objects, flashes and fireballs, and luminescent manifestations of every description are recounted in the annals of Western civilization as far back as Roman times.
Speculation as to their origin was, of course, largely conditioned upon the degree of scientific knowledge at the disposal of the observer.
Generally, however, they were isolated instances, unrelated and devoid of organized study anywhere.
Against this historic background, the controversy which has developed in the United States since 1947
over the so-called flying saucer sightings are absolutely without precedent or parallel.

And a press of accumulation of approximately 800 unexplained reports has not only been accorded the widest possible publicity, intriguing the public everywhere and taxing the credulity of many, but has by now enlisted on a national scale the ingenuity of some of our top airmen, scientists, and military experts.
Curiously enough, it is said that more than 18% of these sightings were reported by trained
military personnel, and some 11% were reported by Air Force pilots alone.
Of all sightings recorded, somewhat less than 15% are reported to be classified as unexplained.
To delve into the mystery of these unexplained phenomena, the resources of the United States
and other nations have mustered at strategic points scores of special cameras, radar installations,
and other detective devices, men by trained personnel.
Meantime, the controversy rages unabated between those who believe that the so-called flying
saucers are facts and those who dismiss them as an illusion.
Tonight, Town Hall is proud to present two distinguished exponents of each of these viewpoints.

Our first guest is Major Donald E. Kehoe, author of Flying Saucers from Outer Space. Born in Iowa, Major Kehoe attended the United States Naval Academy and was commissioned with the rank of lieutenant in the U.S. Marine Corps.
The following year, he finished a training corps for naval aviators at Pensacola.
From 1925 to 1927, he was chief of information of the aeronautics branch of the Department of Commerce
and was assigned as manager of the U.S. tour of the Josephine Ford North Pole plane,
which flew around the country with Floyd Bennett and Bert Blanchard.
In 1949, Major Kehoe was assigned to investigate the flying saucer mystery for True magazine.
The Flying Saucers Are Real was his first book on this subject.
It was followed by Flying Saucers from Outer Space, published in November of this year.
